site.name: FossForThat
site.tagline: Open-source & self-hosted swaps for every paid AI tool
site.description: A living directory of open-source and self-hosted alternatives to popular paid AI tools — with install difficulty, hardware notes, licenses, and what you lose versus the paid version.

tools.name: ChatGPT
tools.summary: Hosted conversational AI with web browsing, memory, voice, and apps.

alternatives.name: Open WebUI
alternatives.minimum_hardware: not published (needs a separate LLM runtime such as Ollama)
alternatives.what_you_lose: No OpenAI-managed models, voice mode, or mobile apps out of the box; you operate the stack and pick models yourself.

alternatives.name: LibreChat
alternatives.minimum_hardware: not published
alternatives.what_you_lose: More setup than ChatGPT; multi-user auth and agents need configuration. Hosted OpenAI-quality models still cost API spend unless you run local weights.

tools.name: Midjourney
tools.summary: Hosted text-to-image with a curated aesthetic and Discord/web workflow.

alternatives.name: ComfyUI
alternatives.minimum_hardware: not published by the UI; image models typically need a CUDA GPU (VRAM depends on the checkpoint)
alternatives.what_you_lose: No Midjourney house style or Discord bot workflow; node graphs have a steep learning curve; model licenses vary (some non-commercial).

alternatives.name: InvokeAI
alternatives.minimum_hardware: not published (GPU recommended for diffusion models)
alternatives.what_you_lose: Less 'one prompt, polished poster' than Midjourney; you manage models, VRAM, and workflows yourself.

tools.name: GitHub Copilot
tools.summary: IDE coding assistant with chat, completions, and cloud agents.

alternatives.name: Continue
alternatives.minimum_hardware: not published (extension; model/hardware depends on the backend you configure)
alternatives.what_you_lose: No GitHub-hosted Copilot models or issue-to-PR cloud agent; quality tracks whatever local or API model you wire up.

alternatives.name: Cline
alternatives.minimum_hardware: not published (extension; model/hardware depends on backend)
alternatives.what_you_lose: Agentic edits need careful review; no Copilot Business admin/policy surface; you pay for or self-host the model.

alternatives.name: Tabby
alternatives.license: custom / mixed (see repo; ee/ may differ)
alternatives.minimum_hardware: not published
alternatives.what_you_lose: Self-hosted completion server for teams; release cadence has slowed; license is mixed (see repo, including ee/).

tools.name: Cursor
tools.summary: AI-native code editor with agents, codebase chat, and tab complete.

alternatives.name: Continue
alternatives.minimum_hardware: not published (runs inside VS Code / JetBrains)
alternatives.what_you_lose: Not a full Cursor fork — you keep your existing IDE; fewer polished agent UX features than Cursor's product.

alternatives.name: Cline
alternatives.minimum_hardware: not published
alternatives.what_you_lose: VS Code extension rather than a dedicated IDE; multi-file agent behavior and pricing differ from Cursor Ultra.

alternatives.name: Aider
alternatives.minimum_hardware: not published (CLI; model-dependent)
alternatives.what_you_lose: Terminal pair-programmer, not a GUI IDE; last repo push as of fetch was 2026-05-22 — verify maintenance before adopting.

tools.name: Jasper
tools.summary: Hosted AI copywriting for marketing teams with brand voice and templates.

alternatives.name: textgen (oobabooga)
alternatives.minimum_hardware: not published (local LLM desktop app; VRAM/RAM depend on model)
alternatives.what_you_lose: No Jasper brand-voice product, campaign templates, or team workspace; you build prompts and templates yourself.

alternatives.name: Open WebUI
alternatives.minimum_hardware: not published (needs a separate LLM runtime)
alternatives.what_you_lose: General chat UI rather than a marketing suite; no Jasper-style brand kit or multi-channel campaign builder.

tools.name: Notion AI
tools.summary: AI writing and Q&A embedded inside Notion workspaces.

alternatives.name: AnythingLLM
alternatives.minimum_hardware: not published (desktop or Docker; plus an LLM)
alternatives.what_you_lose: Does not live inside Notion; you import/sync docs yourself and lose Notion's native editor UX.

alternatives.name: Onyx
alternatives.minimum_hardware: not published
alternatives.what_you_lose: Heavier enterprise-oriented deploy; some connectors/features may be gated — check current docs. Not embedded in Notion.

alternatives.name: Khoj
alternatives.minimum_hardware: not published
alternatives.what_you_lose: AGPL copyleft; personal second-brain focus rather than Notion's collaborative docs UI.

tools.name: ElevenLabs
tools.summary: Hosted TTS, voice cloning, and dubbing studio.

alternatives.name: Chatterbox
alternatives.minimum_hardware: not published (consumer GPU typical for cloning; confirm in project docs)
alternatives.what_you_lose: No ElevenLabs voice library, dubbing studio, or managed uptime; generated audio may include Resemble Perth watermarking.

alternatives.name: Kokoro
alternatives.minimum_hardware: CPU-capable per project README (82M model); GPU optional
alternatives.what_you_lose: Preset voices only — no voice cloning by design; smaller model than ElevenLabs flagship quality for some accents.

alternatives.name: Piper
alternatives.minimum_hardware: not published (designed for on-device / CPU TTS)
alternatives.what_you_lose: Fast local TTS for assistants; fewer studio/cloning features than ElevenLabs.

tools.name: Otter
tools.summary: Meeting transcription with summaries and calendar bots.

alternatives.name: OpenAI Whisper
alternatives.minimum_hardware: not published (CPU works; GPU speeds large models)
alternatives.what_you_lose: Library/CLI, not a meeting bot — no auto-join Zoom/Meet, speaker notes product, or Otter collaboration UI.

alternatives.name: WhisperX
alternatives.minimum_hardware: not published (GPU recommended for speed; diarization may have extra model terms)
alternatives.what_you_lose: Better timestamps/diarization than stock Whisper, still not a meeting assistant with calendar bots.

alternatives.name: whisper.cpp
alternatives.minimum_hardware: not published (CPU-friendly C/C++ port)
alternatives.what_you_lose: Efficient local ASR engine only — you build the meeting workflow around it.

tools.name: Perplexity
tools.summary: AI answer engine with cited web search.

alternatives.name: Vane (formerly Perplexica)
alternatives.minimum_hardware: not published
alternatives.what_you_lose: Search quality depends on SearxNG and the LLM you attach; no Perplexity proprietary index or Pro model lineup.

alternatives.name: GPT Researcher
alternatives.minimum_hardware: not published (docs mention modest server needs in community guides; treat as not published by us unless verified in upstream README)
alternatives.what_you_lose: Report-oriented research agent rather than a polished daily search chat UX.

tools.name: Runway
tools.summary: Hosted AI video generation and editing suite.

alternatives.name: Wan2.2
alternatives.minimum_hardware: not published (large video models; high VRAM typical — check model cards)
alternatives.what_you_lose: Model weights + research code, not Runway's editing suite; slow iteration and ops burden vs hosted Gen-3/4.

alternatives.name: LTX-Video
alternatives.minimum_hardware: not published (check model card for VRAM; commercial terms may include revenue caps)
alternatives.what_you_lose: Open video model rather than a full creative suite; license/revenue terms need a careful read.

alternatives.name: ComfyUI
alternatives.minimum_hardware: not published (video workflows need substantial VRAM)
alternatives.what_you_lose: Flexible node UI for open video models, but no Runway timeline editor or hosted speed.

tools.name: Grammarly
tools.summary: Writing assistant for grammar, tone, and clarity across apps.

alternatives.name: LanguageTool
alternatives.minimum_hardware: not published (self-hosted server; n-gram data optional and large)
alternatives.what_you_lose: Rule-based core is weaker than Grammarly Premium tone/rewrite AI; premium cloud features aren't in the open core.

tools.name: DALL·E
tools.summary: Hosted image generation via ChatGPT and the OpenAI API.

alternatives.name: Stable Diffusion WebUI
alternatives.minimum_hardware: not published (NVIDIA GPU typical; VRAM depends on model)
alternatives.what_you_lose: Maintenance activity has slowed (last push 2026-03-02 as of fetch); no DALL·E 3 ChatGPT integration or OpenAI content policy stack.

alternatives.name: ComfyUI
alternatives.minimum_hardware: not published (GPU VRAM depends on checkpoint)
alternatives.what_you_lose: More powerful and modular, steeper learning curve; you manage models and safety filters yourself.

alternatives.name: InvokeAI
alternatives.minimum_hardware: not published (GPU recommended)
alternatives.what_you_lose: Canvas-oriented local studio; quality depends on which open checkpoints you install.
